'''Valeria Correa Vaz de Paiva''' is a Brazilian [[mathematician]], [[logician]], and [[computer scientist]].
Her work includes research on logical approaches to [[theory of computation|computation]], especially using [[category theory]], 
[[knowledge representation]] and [[natural language]] [[semantics]], and [[functional programming]] with a focus on foundations and [[type theory|type theories]].<ref name="maa">{{citation|url=http://www.maa.org/careers/career-profiles/academia-teaching/valeria-de-paiva|title=Valeria de Paiva|work=Career Profiles|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|access-date=2015-07-24}}.</ref><ref name="mam">{{citation|url=http://www.mathaware.org/mam/2015/highlighted/MAM%202015%20profile_dePaiva.pdf|title=Profile: Valeria de Paiva|work=Mathematics Awareness Month|date=April 2015|publisher=[[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]]|access-date=2015-07-24}}.</ref><ref>Valeria de Paiva {{Official website|https://vcvpaiva.github.io/}}</ref>

==Education==
De Paiva earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1982,<ref name="maa"/> a master's degree in 1984 (on pure [[abstract algebra|algebra]]) and completed a doctorate at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1988, under the supervision of [[Martin Hyland]].<ref name=vphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-213.pdf|title=The dialectica categories|first= Valeria Correa Vaz de|last=Paiva|date=1988|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.315050}}|website=cl.cam.ac.uk|oclc=26346882|issn=1476-2986}}
UCAM-CL-TR-213</ref><ref name=mathgene>{{mathgenealogy|id=49840}}</ref> Her thesis introduced [[Dialectica space]]s, a [[category theory|categorical]] way of constructing  models of [[linear logic]], based on [[Kurt Gödel]]'s [[Dialectica interpretation]].

==Career and research==
She worked for nine years at [[PARC (company)|PARC]] in [[Palo Alto, California]], and also worked at Rearden Commerce and [[Cuil]] before joining Nuance.<ref name="mam"/><ref name="bham"/> She is an honorary [[research fellow]] in computer science at the [[University of Birmingham]].<ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name="bham">[http://www.cs.bham.ac.uk/~vdp/ Home page], University of Birmingham, retrieved 2015-07-24.</ref> She is currently on the Council of the [[DLMPST|Division for Logic, Methodology and Philosophy of Science and Technology of the International Union of History and Philosophy of Science and Technology]] (2020–2023).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dlmps.org/pages/council/council-2020-2023.php|title=DLMPST Website: Council 2020-2023|access-date=16 April 2020}}</ref>

===Selected publications===
* ''Applied Category Theory in Chemistry, Computing, and Social Networks''. (with Baez, Cho, Ciccala and Otter). Notices of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 69, number 2, February 2022.
*''Term Assignment for Intuitionistic Linear Logic''. (with Benton, Bierman and Hyland). Technical Report 262, [[Department of Computer Science and Technology, University of Cambridge|University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory]]. August 1992.
*''Lineales''. (with J.M.E. Hyland) In "O que nos faz pensar" Special number in Logic of "Cadernos do Dept. de Filosofia da PUC", Pontificial Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, April 1991. 
*''A Dialectica-like Model of Linear Logic''. In Proceedings of Category Theory and Computer Science, Manchester, UK, September 1989. Springer-Verlag LNCS 389 (eds. D. Pitt, D. Rydeheard, P. Dybjer, A. Pitts and A. Poigne). 
*''The Dialectica Categories''. In Proc of Categories in Computer Science and Logic, Boulder, CO, 1987. Contemporary Mathematics, vol 92, American Mathematical Society, 1989 (eds. J. Gray and A. Scedrov)
